reason: The wheel looks useful for shaping the clay vessels needed for the first goal.
expectation: I expect to make a shaped clay vessel, though I don't know which one.

alternatives.reason: Clay and planks might make tiles, but I want to start with the vessels.

effect: The bowl is formed but still workable; adding clay to its rim may make another vessel.
reaction: The note about joining more clay makes me curious what shape it will become.
reason: I'll add clay to the bowl while it's still workable, as the result suggests.
expectation: I expect a taller vessel, perhaps a jar.

alternatives.reason: The bowl needs firing eventually, but I want to try shaping it further first.

effect: Adding clay produced a jar, so both vessel shapes are now available for firing.
reaction: The explanation of building up and narrowing the bowl makes the transformation satisfying.
reason: I'll combine sand and clay; it may produce the glaze needed for the vessels.
expectation: I expect a glaze or a material used to make one, though I'm unsure.

alternatives.reason: The jar needs firing, but I want to prepare the glaze first.

effect: The sand and clay made the glaze mixture needed for the vessels.
reaction: That matched my expectation and makes the next preparation clear.
reason: I'll place the glaze at the kiln yard so it can be used on the vessels.
expectation: I expect the glaze to be available at the kiln yard for coating a vessel, though the next step is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The jar also needs to go to the kiln, but I'll prepare the glaze first.

effect: The glaze is at the kiln yard, and either vessel can now be combined with it there.
reaction: The placement opened the coating options as expected.
reason: I'll glaze the bowl to advance the vessel goal.
expectation: I expect a glazed bowl, probably still needing firing.

alternatives.reason: The jar also needs glazing, but I'll start with the bowl.

effect: Glazing the bowl at the kiln also fired it, so the jar may be completed the same way.
reaction: I was surprised that firing happened in the same step.
reason: I'll use the glaze on the jar to advance the vessel goal.
expectation: I expect a fired glazed jar, as with the bowl.

effect: The jar was glazed and fired in one step, completing the vessel goal. The tiled table remains.
reaction: The description of the glaze melting into a glassy surface was satisfying.
reason: Clay and planks may make tiles or a tiled surface for the table.
expectation: I expect a clay tile or a component for the table, though I am unsure.

alternatives.reason: Planks and wood may make the table base, but I will start with the clay.

effect: Clay and planks made a fired tile, providing the surface material for the remaining table goal.
reaction: The explanation of shaping and firing the tile made the combination clear.
reason: Planks and wood seem likely to make the table base needed for the tile.
expectation: I expect a table or table frame that can be fitted with the tile.

effect: The planks and wood made a table, so the tile can now be added to it.
reason: Combining the table and tile directly advances the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect a tiled table that completes the goal.

effect: The table and tile made the tiled table, completing the remaining goal and the chapter.
reaction: The result matched my expectation and brought the sequence to a clear finish.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the jar from the bowl was the most worthwhile moment: the explanation made the change in shape understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the glaze at the kiln was a straightforward preparation with little interest on its own.

surprise.text: Combining the bowl with glaze at the kiln also fired it; I had expected a separate firing step.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary. The tile explanation clarified why clay and planks belonged together.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter: the pottery explanations and the unexpected combined glazing and firing step kept me curious.
